details: An adversarial presentation is at least as hard as a presentation chosen favorably to the learner.
proof: The worst-mistakes game takes the maximum over all presentation sequences, whereas the best-mistakes game permits a favorable choice of sequence.  Taking a maximum over a superset of sequences cannot decrease the optimal worst-case mistake count, so $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{worst}}(\mathcal{H})\ge\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{best}}(\mathcal{H})$.
witness_verification: For C_bw, the best fixed-order transductive mistake bound is 1 while the worst fixed-order bound is 2; sync/verify_best_worst_mistakes_gap.py exhausts the six coordinate orders.
name: Worst Mistakes / Best Mistakes
